items.h: Three catches in return to lineup
items.s: Wilson caught three of six targets for 43 yards in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles. It was Wilson's first game since suffering a finger injury in Week 5 that landed him on injured reserve. He ended up playing 49 of 71 offensive snaps, 39 of which came out wide with 10 in the slot. Wilson had primarily operated as the Steelers' slot receiver prior to his injury, but Germie Bernard has emerged in that role for Pittsburgh. While Michael Pittman (foot) is expected back for Friday's game against the Broncos, DK Metcalf might receive some form of team-imposed discipline after he had an on-field meltdown against the Eagles before being ejected from the game.

items.h: Roman Wilson has three catches in return from IR
items.s: Roman Wilson brought in three passes for 43 yards in Sunday's loss to the Eagles. Wilson returned from an IR stint and had the second-most receiving yards on the team. However, he is still at least WR3 on the depth chart, so he won't be fantasy-viable unless things drastically change.

items.h: Roman Wilson's Fantasy Value Hinges on Teammate's Week 12 Availability
items.s: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Roman Wilson was activated for Week 11 after dealing with a hand injury that had him sidelined for four games, and he returned to action in Week 11, playing 69 percent of the snaps and earning six targets, hauling in three of them for 43 yards (long of 33 yards). It was hard to fully read into Wilson's snap share in Week 11, with DK Metcalf getting thrown out of the game on Sunday and with the NFL reviewing his actions for potential discipline, but Wilson has had his moments prior to his hand injury, catching touchdown passes in back-to-back weeks in Week 3 and Week 4, and earning 5.2 targets on 22.4 routes when active and playing. Wilson's fantasy ceiling…

items.h: Active in Week 11
items.s: Wilson (hand/finger) is active for Sunday's game against the Eagles. The third-year wideout was activated from injured reserve Saturday, foreshadowing his availability for Sunday's contest following a four-game absence. Wilson recorded at least three receptions in his first four games of the season on his way to a 14-188-2 line on 25 targets, and he then failed to reel in the only pass thrown his way in Week 5 against the Colts before exiting that game at halftime with his injury. In his return Sunday against Philadelphia, Wilson should slot into the No. 3 receiver role behind DK Metcalf and rookie Germie Bernard, the latter who leapfrogged Wilson on the depth chart over the last several…

items.h: Roman Wilson Expected to Play Against Eagles
items.s: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Roman Wilson (hand) is expected to play against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 11, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter. Pittsburgh activated Wilson from injured reserve Saturday after a four-game absence. Fellow receiver Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) remains on injured reserve. Wilson practiced in full Wednesday and Thursday. The Steelers estimated full participation on Friday's walkthrough report and listed him as questionable. In the two games before he injured his hand against Indianapolis in Week 5, Wilson caught six passes for 134 yards and scored a touchdown in each game.

items.h: Roman Wilson (finger) activated from IR
items.s: The Steelers activated Roman Wilson from injured reserve. Wilson will officially return for Sunday's game against the Eagles.

items.h: Roman Wilson (finger) expected to play Sunday
items.s: Roman Wilson is expected to return for Sunday's game against the Eagles. Wilson remains listed as questionable and on injured reserve. He'll return to being a WR3/WR4 for fantasy managers.

items.h: Activated from IR
items.s: The Steelers activated Wilson (hand) from injured reserve Saturday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Wilson has missed the Steelers' last four games while on injured reserve due to a left hand injury. He's still listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Eagles, but his activation from IR indicates that the third-year wide receiver will suit up for the Steelers. Michael Pittman (foot) is staying on IR for at least one more week, so as it stands, Wilson slots in as the team's WR3 behind DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard.

items.h: Roman Wilson Set to Come Off Injured Reserve
items.s: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Roman Wilson (hand) is set to come off injured reserve and play Sunday against the Philadelphia Eagles, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. Wilson has missed four games since injuring a finger against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 5. He practiced in full Wednesday and Thursday before Pittsburgh listed him as a full participant on Friday's estimated report following a walkthrough. He was listed as questionable on that report. Wilson scored in consecutive games against the Cincinnati Bengals and Cleveland Browns before the injury, gaining 134 yards on six catches. His two longest catches accounted for 87 of those yards, and he played fewer than 40% of…

items.h: Roman Wilson a Worthy Stash Candidate but a Risky Start if Active in Week 11
items.s: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Roman Wilson (finger) has been on Injured Reserve since suffering a hand injury in Week 5. However, the 25-year-old returned to full participation in practice this week, and he's officially listed as questionable to play in his team's Week 11 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles. Wilson had begun to emerge as a legitimate deep threat in the Steelers offense before getting injured, logging back-to-back games with at least 60 receiving yards and a touchdown. He also earned at least six targets from Pittsburgh quarterback Aaron Rodgers in each of the team's first four games. Wilson may not be able to jump right back into his full workload immediately upon…

items.h: Questionable for Week 11
items.s: Wilson (finger) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports. Both Wilson and Michael Pittman (foot) are listed as questionable but remain on injured reserve. The duo could be activated Saturday if cleared to play against Philly. Wilson has been sidelined since injuring his finger in Week 5 against the Colts.

items.h: Roman Wilson (finger) listed questionable Sunday
items.s: Roman Wilson is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Eagles. Wilson returned to practice this week. He'll have a chance to be activated from injured reserve heading into Sunday.

items.h: Roman Wilson Listed as Questionable for Week 11
items.s: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Roman Wilson (finger) is listed as questionable to come off Injured Reserve and play on Sunday on the road against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 11, according to ESPN's Brooke Pryor. Wilson had his 21-day practice window opened earlier this week, and he was able to practice in full all three days. Both Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) could return from IR this weekend to give veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers more to work with in the passing game. The 25-year-old Wilson has been out since Week 5 against the Indianapolis Colts due to a finger injury. Before getting hurt, the former third-rounder from Michigan caught 14 of his 25 targets for only 188…

items.h: Roman Wilson (finger) logs full practice session Thursday
items.s: Roman Wilson (finger) logged a full practice session on Thursday. Wilson was sidelined for over a month due to a finger issue, but he is now back at practice and was able to log a full session on Thursday. Fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to be relevant even when he's back to full health, however.

items.h: Another full practice
items.s: Wilson (finger) was a full participant in Thursday's practice. With a second full practice under his belt since being designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Wilson looks poised to get activated ahead of Sunday's game against the Eagles. Prior to missing time with a dislocated finger and a fractured digit on his left hand, Wilson had averaged five targets per game over his five appearances, but he could struggle to see that level of volume upon returning. Fellow wideout Michael Pittman (foot) was also a full participant in Thursday's practice and could be a candidate to return from IR this week, and rookie second-round pick Germie Bernard may have performed well enough over…

items.h: Roman Wilson Logs Full Practice on Thursday
items.s: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Roman Wilson (finger) practiced in full on Thursday, per Alan Saunders of Steelers Now. Wilson has been on Injured Reserve since Week 5 with a finger injury, but he could be on track for a return in Pittsburgh's Week 11 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles. Across five games before getting hurt, the 25-year-old recorded 14 catches for 188 yards and two touchdowns on 25 targets. Wilson had begun to emerge as a legitimate deep threat in the Steelers' offense, logging back-to-back games with at least 60 yards and a touchdown before being forced to exit early from Pittsburgh's Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts. In deeper fantasy leagues, Wilson could…

items.h: Practices fully, feels ready to play
items.s: Wilson (finger), who was designated for return from injured reserve earlier Wednesday, was a full participant in his return to practice. Per Mark Kaboly of 93.7 The Fan Pittsburgh, Wilson said after practice that he feels ready to play Sunday against the Eagles, after he dislocated a finger and fractured another digit on his left hand during a Week 5 win over the Colts. So long as Wilson steers clear of setbacks in the Steelers' next two practices, he'll likely be formally reinstated from IR on Saturday.

items.h: Roman Wilson (finger) returns to practice Wednesday
items.s: Roman Wilson returned to practice on Wednesday. Wilson still remains on the Reserve/Injured List. He will have a chance to return in Week 11 for the Steelers.

items.h: Cleared to practice Wednesday
items.s: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said Wednesday that Wilson (finger) has been designated for return from injured reserve, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports. McCarthy suggested earlier in the week that Wilson could be cleared to play Sunday in Philadelphia, and the Steelers' decision to open the wideout's 21-day practice window is the first step in him potentially playing for the first time since Week 5. Through the Steelers' first five games of the season, Wilson recorded 14 receptions for 188 yards and two touchdowns on 25 targets, but it's not clear where exactly he'll settle in the pecking order at receiver once healthy. Like Wilson, veteran wideout Michael Pittman (foot) had his…

items.h: Roman Wilson a Full Participant in Wednesday's Practice
items.s: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Roman Wilson (finger) had his 21-day practice window opened on Wednesday and was able to practice in full, according to Pittsburgh Sports TV's Ashley Wenskoski. The Steelers could be getting some much-needed receiving help for their Week 11 game on Sunday against the hosting Philadelphia Eagles in the form of both Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. (foot), who remain on Injured Reserve. Wilson looks to be on the right track for an official activation by Saturday's deadline, but his fantasy outlook for the week will depend on whether Pittman is activated as well. Before suffering a finger injury that has kept Wilson out since the Oct. 11 win over the…

items.h: Steelers Open 21-Day Practice Window for Roman Wilson
items.s: Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said that the team is opening the 21-day practice window for wide receiver Roman Wilson (finger) on Wednesday, according to Penn Live's Nick Farabaugh. The same can be said for veteran wideout Michael Pittman Jr. (foot), so the Steelers could be getting some much-needed receiving reinforcements for their Week 11 matchup on the road this Sunday versus the Philadelphia Eagles. Wilson, who has been out since Week 5, is not guaranteed to return on Sunday, but he is now eligible to be officially activated from Injured Reserve before Saturday's deadline. The 25-year-old could be a sneaky WR addition off the waiver wire this week in deeper fantasy…

items.h: Roman Wilson (finger) hopeful to return in Week 11
items.s: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said he's "hopeful" Roman Wilson can return in Week 11. Wilson has missed the past month for Pittsburgh as has Michael Pittman Jr. They will both have a chance to return this week. They'll need to be monitored in practice.

items.h: Steelers "Hopeful" to Get Roman Wilson Back This Week
items.s: Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said on Monday that the team is "hopeful" to get wide receiver Roman Wilson (finger) back from Injured Reserve this week to play on Sunday against the Philadelphia Eagles, according to Penn Live's Nick Farabaugh. In addition to Wilson, the Steelers could also be getting Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) back from IR in Week 11, which is good news for a Steelers offense that looked overmatched in their blowout loss to the division-rival Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday night. The 25-year-old Wilson has great chemistry with veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers, but at best, the former third-rounder is a deep-league stash at WR for the stretch run. Wilson was a…

items.h: Candidate to return from IR in Week 11
items.s: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said that he's "hopeful" Wilson (finger) will be able to return from injured reserve for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports. Now that he's spent the required four games on IR while recovering from a finger injury, Wilson is eligible to have his 21-day practice window opened this week. McCarthy expressed similar optimism that fellow wideout Michael Pittman (foot) will be able to come off IR this week, a development that could result in Wilson settling for a lesser role if both receivers are activated ahead of Sunday's contest. Despite a rough start to the season, Pittman signed a two-year, $35 million extension in March…

items.h: Roman Wilson Worth Deep-League Stashes as He Nears Return
items.s: Pittsburgh wide receiver Roman Wilson is worth stashing in some deep fantasy leagues despite him currently being on the injured reserve list. He's eligible to come off that list on November 22, which is Week 11 against Philadelphia. Before landing on IR, Wilson caught 14 of his 25 targets for 188 yards and two touchdowns across five games played. He looked to be emerging after tallying 134 receiving yards and two touchdowns across Weeks 3 and 4, but then got injured in Week 5. That opened the door for Germie Bernard to step into a larger role, so Wilson will not have to fight for snaps and targets with him. Of course, Pittsburgh already has DK Metcalf too, and Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) is…

items.h: Fantasy football Week 6 inactives: Jeremiyah Love, DJ Moore out
items.s: Updated inactives and analysis based on the latest reports and official announcements leading up to kickoff.

items.h: Roman Wilson (finger) placed on IR
items.s: The Steelers placed Roman Wilson on injured reserve. Wilson injured his finger last week. He will miss at least the next four games.

items.h: Lands on injured reserve
items.s: Wilson (finger) was placed on injured reserve Saturday, Ray Fittipaldo of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reports. Wilson already had been ruled out for Sunday's game against Tampa Bay, but the move to IR means that the third-year pro will be required to miss at least four games. Since the Steelers are on a bye for Week 9, the earliest that Wilson can return is Week 11 against the Eagles on Sunday, Nov. 22. He joins Michael Pittman (foot) on injured reserve, which leaves rookie second-rounder Germie Bernard as the Steelers' WR2 behind DK Metcalf for the next few weeks.

items.h: Roman Wilson Placed on Injured Reserve
items.s: The Pittsburgh Steelers placed Roman Wilson (dislocated finger) on Injured Reserve, which will sideline him for at least the next four weeks. Wilson is the Steelers' third-leading receiver, recording 14 receptions for 188 yards and a couple of touchdowns this season. With Wilson unavailable, that will likely mean more targets for rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard, who has totaled 13 receptions for 140 yards on the year. Additionally, fellow Pittsburgh wide receiver DK Metcalf did not practice on Friday due to an illness. Bernard is RotoBaller's 36th-ranked wide receiver and is projected to score nine fantasy points against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers this week. Tampa Bay has allowed an…

items.h: Won't play Week 6 vs. Tampa Bay
items.s: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said Monday that Wilson (finger) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports. Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reported earlier Monday that Wilson is expected to miss at least a couple of weeks due to a finger injury that he sustained during the Steelers' 34-22 win over the Colts on Sunday, so the third-year receiver's absence could extend into Week 7. While the Steelers are without Wilson, Ben Skowronek (leg) and Michael Pittman (foot) for at least Sunday's game at Tampa Bay, quarterback Aaron Rodgers is left with wideouts DK Metcalf, rookie Germie Bernard, running back Jaylen Warren and tight ends Darnell…

items.h: Roman Wilson (finger) ruled out for Week 6
items.s: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said WR Roman Wilson will not play in Week 6 against the Buccaneers. Wilson is expected to miss multiple weeks. He is week-to-week for now.

items.h: Roman Wilson Officially Ruled Out for Week 6
items.s: Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said on Monday that wide receiver Roman Wilson (finger) will not play in Week 6 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, according to Nick Farabaugh of Penn Live. Wilson was worth a look off the waiver wire going into the Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday after the Steelers placed receiver Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) on Injured Reserve. The 25-year-old was not able to take advantage of Pittman's injury, failing to haul in his only target against the Colts before leaving the game with a finger injury and never returning. In the first four games of the 2026 campaign, Wilson caught 26 of his 45 targets for 354 yards and two…

items.h: Roman Wilson (finger) expected to miss multiple weeks
items.s: Steelers WR Roman Wilson is expected to miss a "couple of weeks" after suffering a finger injury on Sunday against the Colts. Wilson is seeking a second opinion after he was originally diagnosed with a dislocated finger. With Michael Pittman Jr. on IR, rookie Germie Bernard will step into a bigger role alongside Pat Freiermuth.

items.h: Expected to miss time
items.s: Wilson (finger) is expected to miss a couple of weeks after exiting Sunday's 34-22 win over the Colts, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports. Wilson is still gathering more information about his injury and is seeking a second opinion, so an official timeline for his recovery may not be determined until he decides on a treatment plan. The third-year wideout out of Michigan logged 20 snaps and was unable to haul in his lone target in Sunday's game before leaving the contest just before halftime. After previously moving Michael Pittman (foot) to injured reserve Saturday, Pittsburgh's receiver depth will be further tested with Wilson likely to be sidelined for at least the team's Week 6 game at…

items.h: Roman Wilson to Miss a Few Weeks
items.s: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Roman Wilson (finger) is expected to miss a few weeks, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. Wilson sustained a finger injury in Sunday's 34-22 win over the Indianapolis Colts. While he's still gathering information and seeking a second opinion, he's likely to miss time. He was held to one target and no receptions in Week 5, but had back-to-back games with more than three receptions, 60 yards, and a touchdown. With Wilson expected to miss a few weeks, rookie receiver Germie Bernard will be the primary beneficiary. Bernard caught six of nine targets for 80 yards in Week 5, playing a career-high 91.7% of snaps. Fantasy managers who currently have Wilson should…

items.h: Roman Wilson (finger) ruled out
items.s: The Steelers have ruled out WR Roman Wilson for the remainder of the game against the Colts with a finger injury. Wilson will finish without a catch on one target Sunday. With Wilson out, Germie Bernard and DK Metcalf will serve as the two top pass catchers for Aaron Rodgers for the remainder of the game.

items.h: The Steelers ruled out Wilson (finger) for the rest of Sunday's game against the Colts, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: With Pittsburgh moving Michael Pittman (foot) to injured reserve Saturday, Wilson appeared headed for a larger role in the receiving corps. Unfortunately for the third-year wideout out of Michigan, he was unable to capitalize in Week 5, as he failed to haul in his lone target before exiting the game late in the second quarter. With Ben Skowronek (leg) also ruled out for the second half, the Steelers will be left with DK Metcalf, Germie Bernard, Kaden Wetjen and Brandon Smith as their available options at receiver.

items.h: Wilson was favoring his hand or wrist as he went to the locker room just before halftime of Sunday's game against the Colts, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports.
items.s: On a play that initially was an 11-yard catch on the field but overturned following review, Wilson appeared to suffer the injury. Its nature isn't known, but Germie Bernard, Kaden Wetjen and Brandon Smith could be in line for WR reps after halftime behind DK Metcalf if Wilson isn't able to return.

items.h: What to know before setting your lineup for Week 5: Is Maye back? Start Wilson?
items.s: Adam Rank catches you up on the vital information and insight needed to make tough lineup decisions in Week 5.

items.h: Fantasy football free agent pickups: Kirk Cousins, Keon Coleman lead top options
items.s: Eric Karabell lists who he thinks are the top available players worth adding for the week ahead.

items.h: Wilson brought in three of six targets for 74 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Thursday.
items.s: Wilson capped off a marathon 17-play opening drive for the Steelers by showcasing his speed, as the second-year wideout scored from 12 yards out on a shovel pass from Aaron Rodgers. Wilson has at least three catches in each of his first four games, and Thursday's yardage total established a new season high after he'd also done so with his 60-yard tally in Week 3. Wilson also has exactly six targets in each contest thus far, cementing him as a key complementary component of the air attack heading into a Week 5 home matchup against the Colts on Sunday, Oct. 11.

items.h: Wilson caught three of six targets for 60 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Bengals.
items.s: Wilson came out of the gates hot Sunday, securing a 38-yard touchdown from quarterback Aaron Rodgers on the team's opening drive of the game. The wide receiver led the team in targets in Week 3, and he has now registered exactly six targets in each of the team's first three contests this season. Wilson has reeled in 11 of 18 targets for 114 yards and a touchdown so far this year.

items.h: Wilson caught five of six targets for 28 yards during the Steelers' 20-3 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
items.s: Wilson stepped into the WR2 role alongside DK Metcalf for Sunday's game due to the absence of Michael Pittman (foot). Wilson responded by leading all Pittsburgh pass catchers in receptions, though he averaged only 5.6 yards per catch in a game where Aaron Rodgers averaged only 4.8 yards per pass attempt. Wilson played 55 of 70 offensive snaps in Week 2, which was tied with rookie second-rounder Germie Bernard for second-most among Steelers wide receivers behind DK Metcalf (68). The Steelers will return home for a Week 3 clash against the Bengals, and Wilson and Bernard would both retain…

items.h: Wilson is set to see more snaps as an outside receiver during Sunday's game against the Patriots, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports.
items.s: Wilson is set to be the No. 2 wide receiver Sunday behind DK Metcalf due to the injury to Michael Pittman (ankle). Wilson saw 54 percent of the Steelers' offensive snaps in the Week 1 win over the Falcons, a number that should increase as the 25-year-old takes on a more critical role. The wide receiver saw six targets in Week 1 and will likely see even more against the Patriots unless the opponent chooses to have standout cornerback Christian Gonzalez follow the third-year player.

items.h: Wilson grabbed three passes for 26 yards and no touchdowns in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Falcons.
items.s: The wide receiver saw six targets in total and played on 37 of 67 offensive snaps. Wilson tied with Jaylen Warren for the second-most targets on the team behind DK Metcalf, so he's clearly a part of the passing game. What he will do with that role moving forward remains to be seen.

items.h: Wilson caught two passes on five targets for 18 yards during the Steelers' 17-0 preseason loss to the Jets on Friday.
items.s: Wilson has been one of the standout players in training camp, but that level of play has not translated to games. Both of the interceptions that Will Howard threw in the second quarter were throws targeted to Wilson, and Mike DeFabo of The Athletic believes that Wilson could have run flatter routes to prevent those turnovers. The 2024 third-rounder is currently listed as the Steelers' WR3 behind DK Metcalf (undisclosed) and Michael Pittman (hamstring), but more lackluster play in games could result in Wilson dropping behind rookie second-rounder Germie Bernard on the depth chart. The…

items.h: Wilson has been the No. 3 wideout with Pittsburgh's first-team offense throughout most of training camp, according to Mike DeFabo of The Athletic.
items.s: The 2024 third-round pick has just 12 catches on 258 career snaps, but he's apparently making a strong case to stay ahead of rookie second-round pick Germie Bernard on the depth chart. With DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman locked in as the top two wide receivers, Wilson probably won't see many targets even if he has a steady role in three-wide sets.

items.h: Head coach Mike McCarthy envisions using Wilson all over the formation, Brian Batko of the Steelers' official site reports.
items.s: "He's done a heck of a job inside, and I haven't even talked to him about this yet, but I think we can start working him a little bit more outside, too," McCarthy said of Wilson. "He can line up at X, Z and F, and so far, he's done exactly what we asked." Wilson is competing with rookie second-round pick Germie Bernard for the third spot on Pittsburgh's wide receiver depth chart behind DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman. Bernard got most of the first-team slot reps at Friday's practice, per Alan Saunders of Steelers Now, while Wilson worked mostly on the outside with the second-team offense,…

items.h: Wilson got the overwhelming majority of reps in three-receiver sets during Wednesday's practice, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports.
items.s: While DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman are entrenched atop the Steelers' WR depth chart, Wilson is looking to secure the WR3 job, with his main competition being second-round rookie Germie Bernard. DeFabo notes that in some instances Wednesday, the Steelers put Wilson and Bernard on the field together, with Bernard playing outside and Wilson in the slot. In any case, the player that emerges as the next option behind the top duo may not have a path to steady volume out of the gate this come Week 1, but that could change should either Metcalf or Pittman miss any time.

items.h: Aaron Rodgers said Tuesday he has high expectations for Wilson this season, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com reports.
items.s: "I expect him to start to make some splash plays," Rodgers said. "He did in the spring. I expect him to have a nice camp." Rodgers was "practically glowing" when talking about Wilson on Tuesday, according to Saunders. Wilson logged just 33 percent of the offensive snaps in his 13 regular-season appearances last season and was essentially running wind sprints, as he was targeted only 21 times across those games and caught 12 passes for 166 yards and two touchdowns. The 2024 third-round pick has a real chance to win the WR3 job behind DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman, however, as Wilson's main…

items.h: Wilson will enter training camp with plenty to prove as he competes for a depth role in Pittsburgh's receiver room, Jack Markowski of SI.com reports.
items.s: Wilson showed momentum during the offseason program and should benefit from a second year working with Aaron Rodgers, as well as the new offensive scheme instituted by head coach Mike McCarthy. Still, with DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman locked into starting roles and rookie second-rounder Germie Bernard pushing for the No. 3 job, Wilson will need a strong camp to secure even a depth role.

items.h: Wilson secured 12 of 21 targets for 166 yards and two touchdowns over 13 regular-season appearances in 2025.
items.s: After missing most of his rookie season in 2024 due to injuries, Wilson had some encouraging performances in 2025, highlighted by a midseason stretch in which he had five performances with double-digit receiving yards in a span of six games. However, his role diminished down the stretch, and he was a healthy scratch in four of the team's last six regular-season matchups. Wilson could have some streaming appeal in 2026, but he'll likely have trouble carving out consistent fantasy relevance throughout the season.

items.h: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday Night Football against the Ravens.
items.s: The wide receiver is now a healthy scratch for the fourth time in five weeks, though he did play nine offensive snaps against the Browns in Week 17. Even with DK Metcalf out due to a suspension, Calvin Austin, Adam Thielen, Marquez Valdes-Scantling, Scotty Miller and Ben Skowronek are ahead of Wilson on the depth chart.

items.h: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's clash against Detroit.
items.s: This is the third straight week that Wilson is a healthy inactive. Prior to this run, he had been seeing steady offensive snaps. However, the Steelers' signing of Adam Thielen appears to have pushed Wilson out of the wideout pecking order.

items.h: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive for Monday night's game against the Dolphins, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
items.s: Wilson will be a healthy scratch for a second consecutive game, coinciding with the addition of veteran wide receiver Adam Thielen to the active roster. Wilson's next chance to play is Sunday against the Lions, but the second-year pro is unlikely to play in that contest unless the Steelers suffer an injury to their wide receiver corps.

items.h: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive Sunday against the Ravens, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com reports.
items.s: The Steelers added Adam Thielen and elevated Marquez Valdes-Scantling from the practice squad this week, giving their wide-receiver corps some depth. That pushed Wilson down the depth chart, though the team opted to make Scotty Miller active ahead of him, after Miller had previously been a healthy scratch. This will mark Wilson's first missed game of the season.

items.h: Wilson failed to secure his lone target during Sunday's 26-7 loss to the Bills.
items.s: Wilson had double-digit receiving yards in five of six appearances following the Steelers' Week 5 bye, but he's failed to secure any of his four targets over the past two games. Over his 12 appearances this season, Wilson has secured 12 of 21 targets for 166 yards and two touchdowns.

items.h: Wilson failed to secure either of his two targets during Sunday's 31-28 loss to the Bears.
items.s: Wilson had recorded at least one catch in each of his last six games, but he failed to establish a connection with quarterback Mason Rudolph in Chicago on Sunday. Wilson was also on the field for just 28 percent of the Steelers' offensive snaps, which was his lowest mark since Week 6. He's shown some glimpses of production this season but hasn't been a very reliable fantasy option.

items.h: Wilson secured one of two targets for 17 yards during Sunday's 34-12 win over the Bengals.
items.s: Wilson was on the field for 57 percent of the Steelers' offensive snaps Sunday, marking just the second time this season that he's played more than half of the team's snaps. His uptick in playing time didn't lead to an increased target share, as he's seen two or fewer targets in eight of 10 of his appearances to begin the season. Wilson's fantasy upside will likely remain limited moving forward, especially if Aaron Rodgers (wrist) is forced to miss time.

items.h: Wilson recorded two receptions on three targets for 35 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 25-10 loss to the Chargers.
items.s: Wilson's three targets were his second-highest mark of the season, though nearly the entirety of his production came in garbage time. He caught a pass from Aaron Rodgers over the middle before turning upfield for a 27-yard score with three minutes remaining in a three-score game to tally his second career touchdown. Wilson has shown occasional signs of progress this season, but he remains a peripheral part of the offense.

items.h: Wilson secured one of two targets for four yards during Sunday's 27-20 win over the Colts.
items.s: Wilson was the Steelers' leading receiver against Green Bay in Week 8 with a season-high 74 yards and a touchdown, but he was held in check a week later. He was held to single-digit yards for the first time since Week 4 while playing 47 percent of the team's offensive snaps, which ranked third among Pittsburgh's wide receivers. Wilson showcased his upside Week 8, but he remains an unreliable fantasy option heading into the second half of the year, and it's possible that the Steelers target a wide receiver ahead of the trade deadline.

items.h: Wilson corralled four of five targets for 74 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-25 loss to Green Bay.
items.s: Wilson waited for the return of fellow wideout Calvin Austin (shoulder) to deliver a standout fantasy performance after struggling in the two games replacing his teammate. The 24-year-old Wilson boosted his final line with a 21-yard touchdown grab in garbage time of Sunday's loss. Wilson hadn't topped 17 receiving yards in any of his previous six outings this year, so fantasy managers shouldn't overreact to what might end up being his best fantasy score of the season.

items.h: Wilson secured both of his targets for 17 yards during Thursday's 33-31 loss to the Bengals.
items.s: Although Calvin Austin (shoulder) remained sidelined for a second consecutive game Thursday, Wilson didn't generate much production in the loss. Over the two games that Austin has missed, Wilson has secured all three of his targets for 29 yards, marking his most productive stretch of the season, but that hasn't been enough to garner much fantasy appeal.

items.h: Wilson secured his lone target for 12 yards during Sunday's 23-9 win over the Browns.
items.s: Wilson was on the field for 15 offensive snaps Sunday, which was his highest mark since the Steelers' Week 2 loss to Seattle. Part of his uptick in playing time was likely due to Calvin Austin (shoulder) being sidelined. Although Wilson had a catch while racking up double-digit receiving yards for the first time this season, he has minimal fantasy value, even if Austin misses more time.

items.h: Wilson wasn't targeted during Sunday's 24-21 win over the Vikings.
items.s: Wilson played double-digit offensive snaps in each of the Steelers' first two games of the season, but he's been held to single-digit snaps in his last two appearances. Although Calvin Austin sustained a shoulder injury during Sunday's overseas victory, he'll have time to recover during the Steelers' Week 5 bye, and Wilson seems unlikely to handle a fantasy-relevant role, especially if Austin is available against the Brown in Week 6.

items.h: Wilson wasn't targeted during Sunday's 21-14 win over the Patriots.
items.s: Wilson was held without a target for the second time in the first three weeks of the regular season, and he was on the field for just 17 percent of the team's offensive snaps in Week 3. Although Wilson appears to be third on the Steelers' depth chart at wide receiver, he's unlikely to have a fantasy-relevant role as long as DK Metcalf and Calvin Austin stay healthy.

items.h: Wilson secured one of two targets for seven yards during Sunday's 31-17 loss to Seattle.
items.s: Although Wilson's workload remained low in Sunday's Week 2 loss, he recorded his first catch of the regular season and also saw a slight uptick in playing time, as he was on the field for 21 offensive snaps compared to 10 during last week's regular-season opener. He saw the third-highest snap count of any Steelers wide receiver, but he's unlikely to have a fantasy-relevant role as long as DK Metcalf and Calvin Austin stay healthy.

items.h: Wilson wasn't targeted during the Steelers' 34-32 win over the Jets on Sunday.
items.s: Wilson had a minimal role for the Steelers when healthy in 2024, and he was utilized sparingly during Sunday's regular-season opener, playing just 10 offensive snaps in the Steelers' victory. The 2024 third-round pick has yet to be targeted in the NFL, and he could have trouble carving out much fantasy production in 2025 as long as DK Metcalf and Calvin Austin remain healthy.

items.h: Wilson recorded two receptions on four targets for 72 yards in Saturday's 17-14 preseason loss to the Buccaneers.
items.s: Wilson got the chance to start with DK Metcalf resting and Calvin Austin (abdomen) sidelined, and he took advantage by creating a few splash plays. Wilson got behind the defense for a 42-yard gain down the middle of the field late in the first quarter and then got wide open on the next drive to tack on another 30 yards. Wilson failed to gain traction in the Steelers' offense as a rookie after battling a few lower-body injuries, but he appears to be getting on track heading into his sophomore campaign.

items.h: Wilson recorded two catches on two targets for 24 yards in Saturday's 31-25 preseason win over the Jaguars.
items.s: Wilson is fighting for a role in Pittsburgh's offense after missing all of his rookie season with lower-body injuries. He's gotten mixed reviews during camp but came into the contest with some momentum, and that continued Saturday -- he recorded catches of 19 and five yards from Mason Rudolph. The Steelers are likely to use an unusual amount of two-tight end formations, leaving Wilson's role uncertain heading into the regular season.

items.h: Wilson opened training camp with the starting offense Thursday, Nick Farabaugh of Penn Live reports.
items.s: Wilson and DK Metcalf took the first reps in both 11 and 12 personnel, with Calvin Austin as the third receiver for three-wide sets (the same role he had last year). It's a sign the Steelers still have high hopes for Wilson, a 2024 third-round pick, after he was either injured or a healthy scratch for nearly all of his rookie season. In addition to Wilson and Austin, the competition for WR snaps behind Metcalf includes Robert Woods, Scotty Miller and Ben Skowronek.

items.h: Wilson may compete for a starting job after the Steelers traded WR George Pickens to Dallas, Chris Adamski of TribLive.com reports.
items.s: Drafted 84th overall last spring, Wilson played just one game as a rookie, missing Week 1 with an ankle injury and Weeks 7-18 with a hamstring injury. In between, he was a healthy scratch four times and played just five snaps in his lone appearance, never truly getting a foot in the door. Steelers GM Omar Khan said in February that Wilson might have contributed in the playoffs had the team advanced beyond the first round, and it now seems he has a shot at the No. 2 WR role for his second pro season. items.h: Steelers general manager Omar Khan said Tuesday at the 2025 NFL Scouting Combine that he has "a lot of confidence" in Wilson (hamstring), and that the wideout was on pace to contribute during the postseason had…
items.s: Wilson, a 2024 third-round pick, was limited to a single regular-season appearance in his rookie campaign, but he at least now appears fully recovered from the hamstring issue that caused him to end the year on IR. He also missed time early in the season with an ankle injury sustained in training camp. If he can put together a strong offseason and remain at full health to enter the 2025 campaign, he could have a big role in Year 2. Wideouts Van Jefferson, Mike Williams and Ben Skowronek are all pending free agents for Pittsburgh.

items.h: Wilson (hamstring) suited up for one regular-season game in 2024 for the Steelers, playing only five offensive snaps and not getting a target.
items.s: Wilson's season wasn't what was expected when he was selected in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft, as the Michigan product suffered an ankle injury in training camp that derailed his season. Even after he recovered, Wilson was a healthy scratch in Week 3 through 5 before making his debut in Week 6 against the Raiders. A hamstring injury then landed him on injured reserve, which is where he ultimately finished the campaign.
